two-sample-z-test.def: A significance test of $H_0: p_1 - p_2 = 0$ about two population proportions, using two independent random samples or two randomly assigned groups. Its standard error uses the pooled proportion $p_c$.

pooled-proportion.def: The proportion of successes in two samples combined, $p_c = \frac{x_1 + x_2}{n_1 + n_2}$. A two-sample z test uses it because the null hypothesis says the two proportions are equal.
